must_fix.title: Contents of a target's own shadow root are hidden when the target is a shadow host
must_fix.evidence: addShadowPath (ariaHideOutside.ts:44-60) starts at the target itself, so `target.shadowRoot` is added to shadowRoots and walk(shadowRoot) hides its children: they have no parentElement and nodeContains(child, target) is false. Probe: shadow support on, button inside host2.shadowRoot, ariaHideOutside([host2]); `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/zzprobe.test.js` printed `A content aria-hidden: true`, while content added to the same shadow root afterwards printed `A added-in-target-shadow aria-hidden: null`, so the result is both wrong and inconsistent. No test covers a target that is a shadow host.

nits: addShadowPath is re-run for every target on every MutationObserver batch that has a childList change, even when the change has nothing to do with the targets' paths; this could be scoped or cached.

report:
I'd hold this PR: one real bug. Tests, lint and the type check all pass, and the rest of the behaviour the issue asks for works in my probes.

**Must fix: content inside a target's own shadow root gets hidden.**
`addShadowPath` (`packages/@react-aria/overlays/src/ariaHideOutside.ts:44-60`) starts its walk at the target itself. When the target is a shadow host (a custom element dialog, for example), its own shadow root lands in `shadowRoots`. `walk(shadowRoot)` then hides every child of that root. Those children have no `parentElement`, so the "inside a visible node" check never matches, and `nodeContains(child, target)` is false. The result is that the dialog's own contents are hidden from screen readers, which defeats the point of the function.

It's also inconsistent: content added later to the same shadow root is left visible, because the observer correctly sees it as inside the target.

I reproduced it with a temporary probe test, `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/zzprobe.test.js` (deleted afterwards). It turns on shadow DOM support, puts a button in `host2.shadowRoot` and calls `ariaHideOutside([host2])`:
```
console.log
  A content aria-hidden: true
console.log
  A added-in-target-shadow aria-hidden: null
```
The fix is to skip a target's own shadow root, and anything inside a target, when collecting shadow roots. A regression test for this case is needed too; none of the new tests use a target that is a shadow host.

What checked out:
- **Tests:** `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays` passes all 197 tests in 10 suites.
- **Lint:** `yarn eslint packages/@react-aria/overlays` is clean.
- **Types:** `yarn check-types` exits 0.
- **Targets in different shadow roots:** an input in a shadow root plus a popover in the light DOM hides the input's shadow sibling and keeps the popover visible (`B sib=true pop=null`).
- **Shadow DOM support off:** behaviour is unchanged.
- **Dependency:** adding `@react-stately/flags` to the package's dependencies matches how `@react-aria/interactions`, `table` and `utils` declare it.
- **Working tree:** `git status` is back to exactly what I found.
